title: Cem Karsan AI’s Debt Bill Could Hit the Stock Market
speaker: Cem Karsan

macro_themes.view: With vol and charm support fading after expiration, markets struggle to rise and stair-step declines make sense.
Refinancing of 2020-21 debt peaks in 2027-28, adding heavy bond supply that pushes yields up.
Hyperscaler capex, bigger than the railroad boom relative to GDP, is turning free cash flow negative and adding debt, with CDS repricing ahead of equities.
Risk-free rates around 5.25% make equity multiples unsustainable; bonds are now a real alternative (reverse TINA).
The endgame is printing money, holding down the long end and buying stocks (e.g. via Trump accounts and share donations), which could extend the AI boom for years.
Widening French spreads and hyperscaler CDS signal a broad debt crisis building at the edges, not only in Europe.

calls.condition: Decline expected to be stair-step (market down, vol down) unless a historic shock triggers dealer short puts and a crash; long-term upside depends on government stepping in to buy stocks.
calls.reason: Post-OPEX, vol/charm support is gone, the index is below its 20-day and failed to reclaim the -1 level; skew is high so hedged customers point to a grinding decline, while debt and rate pressure threaten valuations.
calls.quote: I don't think we're going to fall out of bed, but stair-steps down here would make a lot of sense.

calls.condition: Until a big intervention (money printing, holding down the long end).
calls.reason: A refinancing wave peaking in 2027-28 plus AI-capex debt issuance floods the bond market with supply; the recent dip in yields is a flight to safety.
calls.quote: interest rates, which are, you know, working their way higher broadly, even though we've had this pullback, are now threatening valuations

notes: Host calls the guest 'Jim' and the closing credit says Jim Caron, but the title names Cem Karsan and the content (vol/charm flows, window of non-strength) is Karsan's; speaker kept as Cem Karsan. Date from 'this Monday' with listing 2026-10-20. TNX bias means yields rising (bearish bonds); long-term ES mixed because he expects government support to drive new highs eventually.
